full_judgment:
2. The predecessor of the petitioners filed the above writ petition challenging the order dated 27.2.1982, of the respondent 1 No.1 affirming the judgment and order dated 20.1.1981 of the respondent No.3, in L.A. Case No.60 of 1977-78, and also praying for a direction upon the respondents to release from requisition the properties mentioned in paragraph 3 of the writ petition, hereinafter referred to as property, on the averments that he served as the Principal Officer, Mercantile Marine had no residential accommodation in any city or town in Bangladesh and out of his small savings he purchased the above property measuring 0.40 acres from its original recorded owner Abul Hussain and Hasen Ali by four registered kabalas dated 29.9.1978 and 30.9.1978 at a consideration of Tk.60,000/- and he got possession of the schedule property in the year 1976 and the purchased land being mostly ditches and bushy land, he developed the same by spending a sum of Tk.50,000/- and he also spent huge sum of money for constructing boundary wall around the above property; L.A. Case No.90 of 1964- 65 was started for necessary requisition of land for a housing scheme and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Land Acquisition), Chittagong, the respondent No.5, by Memo No.1980 L.A. dated 31.5.1965 informed the original owners of the above property that the above property was not included in the said L.A. Case and the petitioner also made a query in the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong whereupon he was informed that there was no proposal for future acquisition or requisition of the above property but on a sudden on 12.06.1979 the respondent No.5 issued three notices purporting to be under section 3 of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 and offering advance money in connection with L.A. Case No.60 of 1977-78 and then the petitioner, appearing before the respondent No.5, prayed for release of the above property from requisition submitting that in the notice dated 12.6.1979 the purpose of requisition was mentioned as "Residential Zone under the Scheme Development of Cox's Bazar as Health Resort which cannot he contemplated as public purpose as required under section 3 of the Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 and the respondent No.5 having rejected the above prayer, he preferred Miscellaneous Requisition Case No.151 of 1978 before the Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, the respondent No.3, under section 4A(1) of the above Act 1948 but by order. dated 20.1.1981, Annexure-C to the writ petition, the same was rejected on the ground that acquisition and requisition of the above property was necessary for completion of the housing project started earlier by L.A. Case No.90 of 1964-65 and that there was public purpose behind the said requisition proceeding; thereafter the petitioner in revisional jurisdiction, under section 4A(2) of the above Act; 1948 filed Appeal No. CH-12 of 1981 before the respondent No.1 and the Joint Secretary of the respondent No.1, after hearing, by the impugned order rejected the above appeal but recommending that the petitioner he allotted a plot of land in the proposed residential zone. The respondent No.1 contested the Rule but did not file any affidavit in opposition. 

 3. The High Court Division after hearing, discharged the Rule holding that the respondent No.1 dismissed above L.A Case Appeal No. CH-12 of 1981 on 27.2.1982 but the petitioner moved/filed the writ petition for summery relief only on 23.11.1996, long after 14 years, and in the case of Fazlur Rahman Akhand and live others vs. Government of Bangladesh and others, 52 DLR(AD) 116, this Division held that for seeking summary relief in writ jurisdiction the aggrieved person cannot wait for an indefinite period and must come as expeditiously as possible and in the case of Sarwarjan Bhuiyan and others vs. Government of Bangladesh and others, 44 DLR(HCD)447, the High Court Division, while considering laches on part of the writ petitioner, observed that extraordinary remedy provided in writ jurisdiction is for the vigilant and not for the indolent ones and relief in writ jurisdiction is to be sought immediately after the grievance is caused and accordingly, in the instant case, the petitioner having failed to seek the relief expeditiously, is not entitled to get any relief and further in terms of Article 15 of the Constitution it is a fundamental responsibility of the State to provide to its citizen the basic necessities of life including food, clothing, shelter, education and medical care and in the instant case the above property being needed for the construction of the health resort the acquisition is definitely for a public purpose and it is not for any individual or for a particular group of person or for a commercial purpose.
